# Investor Loan Exchange

> A loan scenario exchange for investment-property lending. A broker submits one loan scenario; it is checked against each lender's niche (product, state, property type, loan size); each fitting panel lender receives one structured rate request; quotes come back to one place, side by side, and the broker chooses who to engage. People and AI agents use the same intake.

Schema version: 1.4 (scenario.schema.json)

## What agents can do here

- Read the scenario format and prepare a loan scenario on a broker's behalf, field for field, validating against scenario.schema.json.
- Intake is the multi-step form at the site (anchor #intake). It has a scenario.json loader above the form: paste a valid file and the form prefills for the human to review. It currently runs in test mode: it validates the entry and shows the exact JSON record, but does not transmit it. When live intake is switched on, submissions will go to an endpoint named on this page.
- The scenario record is lender-facing. The submitter's contact details are collected separately in the form and withheld from lenders until the submitter chooses to engage.
- Name the preparing agent in prepared_by. Never put the borrower's or broker's name in notes.
- ltv, estimated_dscr, loan_to_cost and loan_to_arv are computed by the intake and marked illustrative. An agent may include its own estimates; the intake recomputes them from the numbers.
- Agents prepare and prefill. The human submitter personally reviews the scenario and checks the consent box; never mark consent on a person's behalf, and leave the consent object out of the file - the form adds it when the human submits.
- Quotes and questions always go back to the person on the scenario. The agent prepares; the broker decides.

## Never include in a scenario

- SSNs, dates of birth, or other government identifiers
- Bank account numbers or statements
- Borrower or guarantor names (in notes or anywhere lender-facing)
- Documents of any kind - scenarios only

## Lanes routed

DSCR rental, fix & flip, bridge, ground-up construction, cash-out refinance, and conforming (agency) for investment property only. Owner-occupied (consumer-purpose) scenarios are not accepted.

## Lane-specific fields

- dscr_rental: monthly_rent_usd (required); monthly_taxes_usd, monthly_insurance_usd, monthly_hoa_usd sharpen the DSCR estimate.
- fix_flip: arv_usd and rehab_budget_usd (required); exit_strategy, flip_experience.
- bridge: bridge_exit_strategy and bridge_term (required).
- ground_up_construction: project_budget_usd, build_timeline and guc_exit_strategy (required); land_status optional.
- cash_out_refi: no extra fields.
- conforming_agency: conforming.under_county_limit.

## Preferences by lane

preferences.structure, preferences.rate_type and preferences.prepay_tolerance are optional. Short-term lanes (bridge, ground_up_construction) take month-scale prepay (none, up_to_6mo, up_to_12mo, flexible) and Fixed or Floating rate types; long lanes take year-scale prepay (up_to_3yr, up_to_5yr) and 30-yr fixed or ARM. Values that do not fit the lane are dropped at intake with a note to the reviewer.

## Links

- [Site and intake form](https://thehistoryhotseat.github.io/investor-loan-exchange/#intake): the single intake for people and agents
- [scenario.schema.json](https://thehistoryhotseat.github.io/investor-loan-exchange/scenario.schema.json): JSON Schema v1.4 for one loan scenario
